story.title: The New Play Area
paragraphs_en: Once upon a time, long ago, there was a city. On the outskirts of this city was a slum. The people who lived in it were quite poor. They had no proper roads, markets or schools. The surroundings were filled with filth and dirt. There was always an awful smell in the air. The children were unhappy as they had no place to play. But the worst thing was that a marshland had formed right in the middle of the slum. Since the government did not make any provision to pick up the garbage, all the garbage was thrown into this marsh. The waste water from the homes too accumulated here. More water entered into this pool when it rained.

Things got worse as this dirty pool became a breeding ground for mosquitoes and other pests. This led to dangerous diseases like malaria and dengue. Everyone hated this but did not know what to do. After some time the pool started brimming with water and this dirty, infected water started entering people’s homes. “We hate this water, it is of no use. It has only brought misery and sorrow in our lives,” everyone used to say.

It was only when the elections were held to elect a member of the local municipal area and a resident of their own slum was elected to represent their interests that the people of the slum felt a little relieved. The man elected was Rajendera Singh. He worked as a taxi driver to earn a living, but his passion lay in serving the society. “Now I will use my power to solve the issue of sanitation in my slum.” “The fault lies not with natural resources like water but how we use them. We must use our resources to their fullest potential without exploiting them. There is a difference between using and abusing resources,” he would say. He was also very fond of children. One day he called for a meeting with the children. “Children, I have arranged for your admission at the local government school. But I wish to ask you, what do you miss the most in your lives? What should be developed?”

“A playground! We have nowhere to play. We don’t have proper facilities to spend our free time,” everyone said in unison. Rajendera Singh thought that he had two problems at hand, one of sanitation and the other of recreation. Why not merge both and come up with a solution? Singh liked reading books, too, he believed that the knowledge he gained from books was his real treasure. Even without any access to the internet, he had immense general knowledge. He read about a startup a small company run by a small group of passionate people in Africa that installed pumps under merry-go-rounds. These pumps were installed under polluted water bodies. They also had purifiers within them to purify the water quickly and thoroughly. The energy generated from this entire process of water purifying powered the merry go round to keep operating in circles.

Rajendera Singh found this idea both inspiring and innovative. He went to the post office and bought a Re. 1 postcard and sent it to the startup, requesting for their help. The management of the startup agreed to his request and came to his service. Their services were expensive, but they were more than happy to help. Singh spent all his monthly salary and his funds that he received from the government to pay the startup. They installed big blue pumps and swings on top of them. The swings were bright red, blue, green and yellow. On the request of their parents, tight black seat belts were installed as well, so that the kids wouldn’t fall off!

When the work was done, all the slum kids were called. Now they had recreation facilities as good as the other kids. They didn’t have to wait for the rich kids to get down from the swings so they could use them. The water was no longer smelly. It splashed white and crystal blue. Now the water was being used, not abused. This is the soul of water conservation, using the resource, but sustaining it for a long time - for many people, and many purposes. As the laughter of the kids spread in the air like music, Rajendera Singh felt that he had got his ultimate reward.
